source.title: Hinted Scaling Laws
source.authors: Suze van Adrichem; Luke Bailey; Rohith Kuditipudi; Christine Ye; Neil Band; Ahmed M. Ahmed; John C. Duchi; Percy Liang; Tatsunori B. Hashimoto

record.tranche_reason: The study extends scaling-law prediction to downstream benchmark accuracy, using hinting and joint scale–hint fits rather than testing the original held-out pretraining-loss power laws.
record.gate_note: The study reports downstream accuracy scaling and forecast results. It discusses prior pretraining-loss laws but does not test them. Rankings of nearly indistinguishable models are not rows for the versions below because they do not measure performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
record.test_reason: The study directly tests V6, whether downstream benchmark accuracy can be forecast from model scale. It shows that standard unhinted accuracy-vs-scale laws fail when small models score near zero. Its alternative method, a joint law over scale and hint level, forecasts held-out larger models on Delphi (GSM8K) and post-trained Qwen/Gemma families (AIME, HLE). This is a different method aimed at the same question, so T2 fits better than T3. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that jointly modelling hint level and scale gives more accurate downstream accuracy forecasts than scale alone, which fails when small models score near zero, and enables sample-efficient ranking. They flag the scarcity of open scaling ladders (only Delphi is a single-recipe ladder) and say the joint law is an imperfect approximation.
record.recipe_differences: The original sources study held-out pretraining loss and compute-optimal training allocations. This paper studies downstream benchmark accuracy with hinting and fits joint floored sigmoid laws in scale and hint level.
record.method_sensitivity: Forecast performance varies with hinting method, teacher choice, seed averaging, and the training models included in a forecast. The paper reports that raw logit mixing produces an inverted scale trend for Qwen2.5; standard-deviation rescaling improves its forecast error. It also reports that masking and truncation can under- or over-forecast beyond 10x compute when used individually.

fits_no_version.finding: Hinted rollouts rank near-zero, nearly indistinguishable models with fewer rollouts: Kendall's tau improves by 0.33 on AIME and 0.27 on HLE at one rollout per problem.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hinted evaluations reduce the sampling budget needed to rank models by unhinted accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Bits-per-byte against parameter count on post-trained families fits poorly: the fitted floor L∞ hits its lower bound of zero in three of four families, so the floor is not identified.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss-proxy power laws for post-trained families are poorly identified with few models.

record.problems: The authors identify scarcity of open-source scaling ladders as a main limitation: only Delphi is explicitly a scaling ladder trained with one data recipe among the five model families. The joint law is acknowledged to be imperfect. The paper reports poor forecasts for raw within-family logit mixing on Qwen2.5 and for the two-stage baseline in the tested settings. Some forecasts depend on seed averaging, and the ranking analysis uses different roll-out counts across benchmarks.
record.rows_left_out: Pointwise accuracy values and forecast errors shown only as curves or cells in Figs. 2–20 are not individually extracted; the record includes the textually stated aggregates and outcomes. Ranking results are excluded from rows because they do not measure accuracy against model scale or pretraining loss.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a power law in parameters, tokens or compute. The only loss power law fitted is on GSM8K solution-trace bits-per-byte, and only as a forecasting baseline.
Extrapolation of pretraining-loss power laws to much larger runs.
Effect of architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
Other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer scaling.
Predictability against pretraining loss proper. Benchmarks other than GSM8K, AIME and HLE, and families beyond Delphi, Qwen2.5/3/3.5 and Gemma-3.
Dependence of loss exponents or compute-optimal splits on fitting and setup choices.

missing.what: Unhinted standard-scaling-law forecast errors as their own rows: 13-point under-forecast (12 points with fits up to 1e22), 21-point median error, 88.2 points on Qwen2.5 AIME.
Logit-mixing joint-fit MAE of 1.7 points on Delphi, equal to the individual-slice fits.
Masking and truncation used alone respectively under- and over-forecast substantially beyond 10x compute.
Pass@k used as a hinting method generally beats the baseline but underperforms the hinting ensemble. The answer-mixing control forecasts terribly.
Forecasts for the remaining family/benchmark pairs (Qwen3 AIME; Qwen2.5 and Gemma-3 HLE).

record.verdict_notes: The verdicts rest on hinted rather than raw accuracy, so V6 support is conditional on the hinting construction. The study's own baseline shows raw accuracy-vs-scale laws are unreliable in the near-zero regime. R8/R9 cover only AIME on three families, with the std-rescaling correction chosen post hoc. The post-trained families are not controlled ladders (C is log parameters, recipes vary).

versions.untested_parts: Power-law held-out pretraining loss against parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on small runs predict held-out pretraining loss at much larger scales.
The compute-optimal parameter/token allocation or its growth with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Other modalities and the listed alternative training regimes, including repeated data, fine-tuning, and transfer.

The study tests downstream benchmark accuracy against model scale, not against pretraining loss; it does not establish predictability for downstream tasks beyond the benchmarks and model families evaluated.

It does not test dependence of pretraining-loss exponents or compute-optimal allocations on parameter counting, training schedule, or data. Its fitting and forecasting limitations concern downstream accuracy laws.

source_check.correct: For the seed-averaged forecasting operation, state=observed: mean forecasting error is 3.3 percentage points across nine training sets. The original-seed-only comparator has 10.2-point mean error. The 0.5–2% unhinted accuracies and 2.5% fitted floor describe the low-scale regime, not failure of the seed-averaged forecast.

rows.value: Approximately 16–24 percentage points; forecast is essentially a flat line at 0
rows.note: The paper attributes the failure to fitting the accuracy sigmoid on near-zero accuracy values.
rows.check: The soft metric is bits-per-byte on GSM8K solution traces, not held-out pretraining loss. The row bears on V6's 'predictable with loss' clause only through this proxy. It is a comparator method fit on Held's ten single-seed models.

rows.subject: Delphi ladder models
rows.operation_detail: Forecast GSM8K accuracy with a two-stage bits-per-byte method anchored by external reference models
rows.value: The intermediate sigmoid fits well, but the compute-to-bits-per-byte law becomes inaccurate with enough held-out models, leading to poor overall predictions
rows.note: The authors note that small bits-per-byte prediction errors can produce large accuracy errors near the steep part of the sigmoid.
rows.check: No number is extracted. Two findings need separating: the BPB-to-accuracy sigmoid fits well when anchored by external models, while the compute-to-BPB extrapolation fails.

relationships.condition: Hinted accuracy (masking/truncation ensemble; logit mixing with a shared external teacher on Delphi), fit on small family members
relationships.reason: The joint scale–hint law fits with roughly 3-point MAE (R1, R2). Forecasts of held-out larger models land within about 3–4 points: 3.3-point mean on Delphi (R3); within 3 points at 1e23 from at most 1e20 (R4); 4.3-point median and 17 of 19 panels beating baseline (R5); 3.0 points on Qwen2.5 AIME (R6).
relationships.display_finding: The joint law fitted with roughly 3-point MAE; held-out forecast errors were 3.3 points on average on Delphi, within 3 points at 1e23 from at most 1e20, a 4.3-point median elsewhere and 3.0 points on Qwen2.5 AIME, with the law beating the baseline in 17 of 19 panels.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Standard unhinted accuracy-vs-scale laws when the smaller models score near zero
source_check.reason: For this isolated condition, predictability fails explicitly: R4–R6 report a 13-point under-forecast, 21-point median error and 88.2-point error. These show an absent predictive effect where unqualified V6 would assert it.

relationships.condition: Choice of forecasting setup: seed averaging, teacher choice and logit-mixing rule, and the two-stage bits-per-byte route
relationships.reason: Single-seed fits give 10.2-point mean error (R7). Raw within-family logit mixing inverts the scale trend for Qwen2.5, improved by std rescaling (R8, R9). The two-stage BPB forecast is flat at 0 with 16–24-point error (R10), or inaccurate even with reference anchoring (R11).
relationships.display_finding: Single-seed fits had 10.2-point mean error, raw logit mixing reversed Qwen2.5's scale trend until standard-deviation rescaling, and two-stage bits-per-byte forecasts stayed at zero with 16–24-point errors or remained inaccurate after reference anchoring.

tranche.reason: The study tests scale-based predictability using a different forecasting method: joint scale–hint accuracy laws with explicit larger-model holdouts.

source_check.notes: R1–R2 are fit errors, not extrapolation errors. Separate R8 by family and retain failed baseline forecasts as standalone results; GSM8K solution-trace bits-per-byte is not held-out pretraining loss.

statements.correction: Delphi: pretrained ladder; GSM8K; solution-conditioned shared-teacher logit mixing; mean forecasting error=3.3 percentage points across nine training sets. Code and data linked. Ranking uncertainty: Bonferroni-corrected 95% confidence intervals for pairwise accuracy differences.
statements.problem: The 3.3-point Delphi result concerns a pretrained scaling ladder, so describing this example as a post-training forecast is inaccurate. The study reports ranking uncertainty, but no uncertainty interval accompanies the 3.3-point forecasting result.
